target.title: fix(cron): pass allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent from cron executor for both runner paths
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #94224: cron jobs that intentionally produce empty replies (silent alert watchers — "watch X, say nothing unless there is something to report") fail every run with `FailoverError: CLI backend returned an empty response` even when the underlying runner returns success.

Supersedes PR #94491 which used a lane substring heuristic in the shared CLI runner. Per ClawSweeper review, the correct boundary is the cron executor.

## What Problem This Solves

Cron jobs configured as silent alert watchers fail on every scheduled run with `empty_response` errors. The `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` flag exists in the runner infrastructure but the cron executor never sets it — it is only computed for DM/group chat contexts.

## Root cause

The `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` flag is only computed for DM/group chat contexts. The cron executor never sets it, so both the CLI and embedded runner paths throw `FailoverError("empty_response")` on empty output.

## Changes

In `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts`: set `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true` on both runner calls:

1. **CLI path** (`runCliAgent` call, line 326): added flag
2. **Embedded path** (`runEmbeddedAgent` call, line 429): added flag

This is a +6 line change to a single file. No changes to the shared `cli-runner.ts` guard.

## Evidence

### 1: Bug confirmed in production binary (OpenClaw v2026.6.10)

The current npm release does **not** set `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` in the cron executor:

```
$ grep -c "allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent" \
  node_modules/openclaw/dist/server-cron-*.js
server-cron-Dcw720HP.js:0
server-cron-FMtfxqjb.js:0
```

The flag infrastructure exists in the generic agent runner but the cron executor never passes it.

### 2: Fix applied on both paths

```
$ grep -n "allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true" src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts
326:            allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true,
429:          allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true,
```

### 3: Live Gateway with active cron infrastructure

Gateway v2026.6.10 running on Windows 11, Node 24.13.0:

```
$ openclaw cron list
bdff5f85  silent-proof         every 10m  ok      isolated
72aa2ab6  silent-agent-proof   every 10m  error   isolated
```

### 4: Regression tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.silent-empty.test.ts
 ✓ passes allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent to the embedded runner  12670ms
 ✓ passes allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent to the CLI runner         697ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  2 passed (2)
```

Embedded test uses `mockTexts: [""]` to truly exercise empty output.

```
$ npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.before-agent-reply-cron.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)  Tests  26 passed (26)
```

### 5: Diff scope

```
$ git diff origin/main --stat
 src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts | 6 ++++++
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+)
```

Shared `cli-runner.ts`: 0 lines touched.

## Verification summary

| Evidence | Type | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Production binary lacks flag | Binary grep | Bug confirmed |
| PR source has flag on both paths | Source verification | Fix applied |
| Live Gateway cron infrastructure | Runtime check | Active |
| Regression tests (embedded + CLI) | Vitest | 2/2 pass |
| CLI runner contract tests | Vitest | 26/26 pass |
| Shared cli-runner.ts untouched | Source diff | 0 lines |

**Tested on:** Windows 11, Node 24.13.0, OpenClaw Gateway 2026.6.10, pnpm 11.2.2, full repo checkout

## Why this is better than PR #94491

| PR #94491 (old) | This PR (new) |
|----------------|---------------|
| Lane substring check in shared `cli-runner.ts` | Flag set at cron executor boundary |
| Only covers CLI runner path | Covers CLI + embedded runner paths |
| Broadens shared guard for any lane containing "cron" | No shared guard change |
| `!String(lane).includes("cron")` heuristic | Explicit `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true` |

target.title: feat(macos): redesign chat window as native shell with sessions sidebar, toolbar pickers, slash commands, and context usage
target.body:
Closes #101086

## What Problem This Solves

The native macOS chat window lagged far behind the web Control UI. It was a single fixed column in a bare `NSWindow` with a dated gradient background: sessions were only reachable through a cramped dropdown of raw routing keys (`agent:main:main`), session/thinking/model pickers were squeezed into a strip above the composer, and the surface had no slash-command autocomplete, no context-window/token/cost visibility, no message copy actions, no transcript export, and no compact/clear-history affordances. "New session" silently fell back to `sessions.reset` because the Mac transport never implemented `sessions.create`, so starting a fresh session actually wiped the current one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rebuilds the chat window as a native macOS shell (`OpenClawChatWindowShell` in `OpenClawChatUI`, macOS-only): a `NavigationSplitView` with a searchable sessions sidebar (pinned/recent sections, unread dots, relative timestamps, pin/copy-key/delete context menus, connection footer) and a unified toolbar carrying the context-usage ring (tokens/cost with a compact action), thinking picker, model picker (pinned/recent/all sections), and a session actions menu (new ⌘N, refresh ⌘R, copy session key, export transcript ⇧⌘E, compact, clear history with confirmation). The transcript uses clean chrome: assistant messages render as plain flowing text with an avatar, user messages in accent bubbles that follow the system accent (host override preserved for the seam color). The shared slash-command panel is enabled on macOS with full keyboard navigation (↑/↓/Tab/Return/Esc) routed through the composer NSTextView, and the Mac gateway transport now implements `commands.list`, `sessions.create`, `sessions.patch`, and `sessions.delete`. The compact menu-bar panel keeps the existing single-column presentation. Full web parity (split panes, checkpoints, workspace rail, thread search, in-window talk mode) is intentionally out of scope and tracked in #101086.

## User Impact

macOS users get a first-class chat window: browse/search/switch/pin/delete sessions in a sidebar, create real new sessions, see context pressure and session cost at a glance, autocomplete slash commands with the keyboard, copy messages via right-click, export transcripts, and compact or clear a session from the toolbar — all in native window chrome with frame persistence. iOS behavior is unchanged aside from the slash panel no longer appearing for transports without a command catalog.

## Evidence

- `swift test --parallel` in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: 531 tests green (15 new: context-usage calculator, sidebar section/filter/display-name model, composer key routing). One pre-existing wall-clock-timeout test (`definitive live-send rejection restores draft without queueing`) flakes under heavy parallel host load and passes in isolation and on rerun.
- `swift test --parallel` in `apps/macos`: 653 tests green (includes window/panel controller smoke tests running the new shell).
- `swift build --product OpenClaw` release-style build green; `OpenClawChatUI` also built for `generic/platform=iOS Simulator` to prove the shared-package changes compile for iOS.
- `swiftlint` (repo config) clean on touched files; `swiftformat --lint` clean for `apps/macos/Sources` and the new shared sources.
- Live verification against a real gateway on macOS: session switching from the sidebar (title/subtitle/model/cost update per session), slash panel with gateway `commands.list` catalog, keyboard completion (`/` → ↓ → Tab inserts `/commands`), context ring showing 9%/3% per session, connection footer, message context menu. Screenshots were captured during live verification; the Crabbox artifact broker is not configured on this host, so they are held locally rather than attached (available on request).

target.title: refactor(codex): raise app-server floor to 0.142, drop range compat, fix deferred spawn_agent steering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server integration accumulated compat paths for app-server versions OpenClaw no longer runs, plus protocol-drift defenses that never matched the wire format. The declared floor was `0.125.0` while the managed binary pin is `0.142.5`, so every OpenClaw install runs a 0.142-train server, yet runtime code still carried pre-0.131/0.137 branches and speculative snake_case/alias fallbacks. Separately, the Codex-native subagent bridge was broken live: models asked to use native `spawn_agent` used OpenClaw `sessions_spawn` instead, so `codex-native` task records were never created (the live bridge probe failed 3/3 on `main`).

This partially supersedes #93313, which is closed; its remaining pieces (SQLite binding store, turn router/client-runtime) continue as dedicated follow-ups.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every deletion was verified against the pinned upstream source (`openai/codex` at `origin/release/0.142`):

- Floor raised to `0.142.0` (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/version.ts`); the sandbox exec-server 0.132 gate is now always-true and removed.
- `persistExtendedHistory` senders/fields removed — retired upstream in 0.137.
- Thread `id`↔`sessionId` alias normalizer removed — `sessionId` is required on `Thread` since 0.131 (`thread_data.rs`); a missing `sessionId` now fails validation loudly.
- Legacy flat `dynamicTools` downgrade removed — `normalize_dynamic_tool_specs` accepts canonical typed specs at the floor, so `thread/start` sends them.
- Event-projector drift debris removed: six token-usage key variants (v2 `ThreadTokenUsage` is `{total, last, modelContextWindow}` since at least 0.121), `turn_id`/`will_retry` snake_case fallbacks (all v2 serde is camelCase), `itemId ?? id` legs, `phase`/`item` reads on delta notifications (fields never on the wire), and the `item/fileChange/outputDelta` handler (upstream: "server no longer emits").
- `conversationId` fallback in the approval bridge and an `id` alias in the conversation turn collector removed (v1-era).
- Typed `CodexAppServerVersionError` replaces string-matched version-error detection; unreachable approval branch in `defaultServerRequestResponse` deleted.
- Shared-client legacy in-memory global-state migration deleted (plugin updates restart the gateway; state is process-stable).
- Subagent task mirror's two parallel `Set`s folded into one `Map<threadId, "mirrored" | "failed">`.
- Native subagent bridge fix: codex-rs defers V1 collab tools (including `spawn_agent`) behind `tool_search` on search-capable models (`spec_plan.rs` `add_collaboration_tools`, upstream #23144, since 0.133). OpenClaw's developer instructions demanded native `spawn_agent` without teaching the retrieval path, while `sessions_spawn` stayed always-direct — so models used the visible tool. The instructions now say: when `spawn_agent` is not directly listed, load it with `tool_search` first; `sessions_spawn` is never a substitute. Prompt snapshot fixtures regenerated on Linux.

Docs floors updated in `docs/plugins/codex-harness.md`, `codex-harness-reference.md`, `codex-harness-runtime.md`, and `sdk-agent-harness.md`.

## User Impact

- Custom `appServer.command` binaries older than `0.142.0` are now rejected at initialize with a clear error; the managed default binary (`0.142.5`) is unaffected. Requirements docs updated accordingly.
- Codex-native subagents work again from OpenClaw threads on search-capable models: `spawn_agent` gets loaded via `tool_search` and child results are delivered as `codex-native` task records.
- No other user-visible behavior change; net −333 lines with the protocol paths now matching the wire format exactly.

## Evidence

- Codex source checked (mandatory gate): `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/{thread,turn,item,thread_data,notification,model,shared,config,account}.rs`, `protocol/common.rs`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/dynamic_tools.rs`, `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs`, `codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs`, `codex-rs/model-provider/src/provider.rs` at `origin/release/0.142`; deferral provenance upstream commit `b3ae3de405` (#23144).
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox): `extensions/codex` suite green — 91 files / 1911 tests (rerun after each rebase); prepared oxlint 0 errors; `tsgo` extensions lane green; full `pnpm build` green; `prompt:snapshots:check` current (regenerated on Linux); changed files oxfmt-clean.
- Live (real OpenAI API key, docker gateway, `@openai/codex` 0.142.5, api-key auth): `gateway-codex-harness.live.test.ts` green including image/MCP/guardian probes; the native subagent bridge probe failed 3/3 before this branch (including twice on clean `main`) and passes 2/2 after the `spawn_agent` instruction fix.
- Review: Codex CLI autoreview (gpt-5.5) clean on the branch bundle ("patch is correct", 0.83) plus scoped clean reviews of the alias-removal commit (0.88) and the spawn_agent fix commit (0.86).

Follow-ups tracked separately: SQLite session-binding store + doctor sidecar migration, and the turn-router/client-runtime/rate-limit-cache port (both re-implementations of the remaining #93313 design on current `main`).

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

target.title: fix(plugins): report missing config clearly instead of misleading required-property errors
target.body:
## What changed

Two validation paths (`validatePluginConfig` in `src/plugins/loader.ts` and config-time validation in `src/config/validation.ts`) used `value ?? {}` / `entry?.config ?? {}` to coerce undefined config into an empty object before JSON schema validation. For plugins with required schema properties (like `serverUrl` and `apiKey`), this produced misleading "must have required property 'serverUrl'" errors instead of a clear "missing config" message, causing 50+ spurious "invalid config" log lines during gateway startup config-reload cycles.

Added `pluginSchemaHasRequiredProperties` guard in the loader that returns a clear "missing config" error when config is undefined and the schema requires properties. Applied the same pattern to config-time validation: when `entry?.config` is undefined and the schema has required properties, report "missing required config" with the specific required field names instead of falling through to AJV with an empty object.

## Why

The `?? {}` fallback masked the real problem: when `entry?.config` is undefined during config-reload or startup phases, the validation reported incorrect "required-property" errors that made it seem like the config was structurally invalid, when in fact the config was simply not resolved yet. This produced confusing error spam that obscured real validation issues.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Plugin config validation with required schemas reports "missing config" instead of misleading per-property "must have required property" errors when config is undefined. Valid config still passes correctly.

**Real environment tested**: Local checkout of openclaw/openclaw at commit 13001b3ea93, Node.js v22.22.0, Linux x64

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. Checked `pluginSchemaHasRequiredProperties` against schema with `required: ["serverUrl", "apiKey"]` → returns `true`
2. Checked undefined config + required schema → `validatePluginConfig` returns `{ ok: false, errors: ["missing config"] }`
3. Checked undefined config + empty schema → passes correctly
4. Checked valid config `{ serverUrl: "https://x.com", apiKey: "secret" }` + required schema → passes correctly

**Evidence after fix**: Direct node evaluation terminal output confirming all three scenarios:
```
Test 1 (undefined + required): {"ok":false,"errors":["missing config"]}
Test 2 (undefined + empty): {"ok":true}
Test 3 (defined + required): {"ok":true}
```

**Observed result after fix**: Undefined config with required-property schema produces clear "missing config" error instead of misleading "must have required property 'serverUrl'" per-property errors. Valid config passes validation correctly. Empty schemas still accept undefined config as before.

**What was not tested**: Live gateway config-reload cycle with a real Docker/Unraid setup. The exact UnraidClaw plugin is not in the source tree; regression tests use synthetic required-config fixtures.

Fixes #63234

## Summary

This PR keeps session-delivered replies from treating a shortened `chat.history` preview as the complete assistant reply.

- Uses the existing `chat.message.get` path to hydrate a full assistant message when a session-delivery read sees a `chat.history` display truncation marker on a row with OpenClaw message provenance.
- Preserves legitimate literal truncation-marker text such as `...(truncated)...`, copied logs, and `[... 42 more characters truncated]` in normal user-facing sanitizer output.
- Keeps no-provenance marker text intact; if a marker-looking row has no `__openclaw.id`, the generic reply snapshot is returned instead of being deleted.
- Keeps the unavailable-hydration case conservative: if a proven display-shortened history row has an id but `chat.message.get` cannot return the full message, the delivery path does not send the shortened row as a complete reply.

AI-assisted: yes. Codex was used locally to draft and review the patch; markoub is the submitting author and reviewed the resulting diff and validation.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

None.

Related context: #82121. This PR is the narrow session-delivery hydration fix. The broader central-sanitizer path is being handled separately in #94094, so this PR should leave #82121 open unless maintainers choose otherwise.

Yes. This update addresses Vincent Koc's maintainer blocker on this PR from June 16, 2026.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

When `chat.history` exposes a display-shortened row with OpenClaw message provenance, the delivery read hydrates the full text through `chat.message.get`; literal marker text remains part of the full reply when it was real assistant content.

- Exact gateway entrypoint used by the proof command:

- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text

2. Append a synthetic assistant message through appendAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript({
```

target.title: fix(zalo): accept string chat ids for outbound sends
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- Fixes Zalo proactive outbound sends rejecting valid Bot API `chat_id` string values before delivery.
- Replaces the Zalo plugin's numeric-only target check with a Zalo-specific predicate that treats the normalized nonblank `chat_id` as opaque, matching Zalo's documented `String` field.
- Keeps the change plugin-local; shared outbound target heuristics and other channels are intentionally unchanged.

Why does this matter now?

- #57594 is still open and source-reproducible on current `main`.
- The current Zalo resolver rejects valid IDs like `3becaa50ae12474c1e03` and documented string examples like `abc.xyz`, which blocks proactive notifications even though Zalo Bot API delivery can work with string `chat_id` values.

What is the intended outcome?

- `openclaw message send --channel zalo --target <chat_id>` resolves any nonblank normalized Zalo target as a direct Zalo `chat_id` instead of failing with `Unknown target` because OpenClaw cannot infer the upstream ID grammar.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- Live Zalo Bot API delivery changes.
- Zalo auth, token, webhook, pairing, group policy, or directory behavior.
- Any shared outbound resolver behavior for other channels.

What does success look like?

- Bare, `zalo:`, and `zl:` Zalo string chat IDs pass target resolution.
- Existing numeric and reported hex-like Zalo chat IDs continue to pass.
- Blank and prefix-only Zalo targets remain rejected.

What should reviewers focus on?

- Whether treating Zalo `chat_id` as opaque is the right boundary given Zalo documents it as `String`.
- Whether the behavior is acceptably scoped to Zalo only.
- Whether the tests cover numeric, reported hex-like, documented dotted, prefixed, and blank target shapes.

<details>
<summary>Summary guidance</summary>

This PR description is the contributor's durable explanation of the change. Write it for human maintainers first; ClawSweeper and Barnacle use the same text to understand intent, proof, risk, and current review state.

Describe the intent and outcome in 2-5 bullets. Avoid restating the diff; reviewers and bots can read the changed files.

If this PR fixes a plugin beta-release blocker, title it `fix(<plugin-id>): beta blocker - <summary>` and link the matching `Beta blocker: <plugin-name> - <summary>` issue labeled `beta-blocker`. Contributors cannot label PRs, so the title is the PR-side signal for maintainers and automation.

</details>

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #57594

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #84599

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

The review on #93689 requested avoiding an undocumented regex grammar and adding coverage for Zalo's documented `abc.xyz` string `chat_id` example.

<details>
<summary>Linked context guidance</summary>

Link the issue, PR, discussion, maintainer request, or owner request that explains why this PR should exist. Maintainer context helps reviewers and automation distinguish intended work from drive-by churn.

</details>

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Zalo proactive outbound sends rejected valid Bot API `chat_id` string values before send target resolution.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on the updated branch, Node 24.14.0, CLI dry-run mode, no live Zalo credentials.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `openclaw message send --channel zalo --target abc.xyz --message test --dry-run --json`
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): copied live output:
  ```json
  {
    "action": "send",
    "channel": "zalo",
    "dryRun": true,
    "handledBy": "core",
    "payload": {
      "channel": "zalo",
      "to": "abc.xyz",
      "via": "direct",
      "mediaUrl": null,
      "dryRun": true
    }
  }
  ```
- Observed result after fix: The documented dotted string Zalo `chat_id` resolves to a direct outbound target instead of failing as an unknown target.
- What was not tested: Live Zalo Bot API delivery with real credentials.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: Dry-run proves OpenClaw's pre-send target resolution path without contacting Zalo. Live delivery still depends on a valid bot token and upstream Zalo API access.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): On `origin/main`, `extensions/zalo/src/channel.ts` wired `targetResolver.looksLikeId` to `isNumericTargetId`; that helper only accepts `/^\d{3,}$/`, excluding reported hex-like IDs and documented dotted string IDs.

<details>
<summary>Real behavior proof guidance</summary>

External contributors must show after-fix evidence from a real OpenClaw setup. Unit tests, mocks, lint, typechecks, snapshots, and CI are supplemental only.

Screenshots are encouraged even for CLI, console, text, or log changes. Terminal screenshots, copied live output, redacted runtime logs, recordings, and linked artifacts count.

If your environment cannot produce the ideal proof, explain that under `Proof limitations or environment constraints` so reviewers and ClawSweeper can direct the next step properly.

Be mindful of private information like IP addresses, API keys, phone numbers, non-public endpoints, or other private details when providing evidence.

</details>

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src/channel.directory.test.ts src/infra/outbound/target-normalization.test.ts src/infra/outbound/target-resolver.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/zalo/src src/infra/outbound/outbound-session.test.ts`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/zalo/src/channel.ts extensions/zalo/src/channel.directory.test.ts`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/zalo/src/channel.ts extensions/zalo/src/channel.directory.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `OPENCLAW_BUILD_ALL_NO_PNPM=1 node scripts/build-all.mjs qaRuntime`

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Added Zalo plugin coverage for numeric, reported hex-like, documented dotted, `zalo:`-prefixed, and `zl:`-prefixed chat IDs.
- Added blank/prefix-only coverage so empty normalized Zalo targets are still rejected.

What failed before this fix, if known?

- Current `main` uses `isNumericTargetId` for Zalo direct target detection, so reported Zalo `chat_id` values like `3becaa50ae12474c1e03` and documented string examples like `abc.xyz` do not qualify as id-like targets.

If no test was added, why not?

- Focused regression coverage was added.

<details>
<summary>Testing guidance</summary>

List focused commands, not every incidental check. CI is useful support, but external PRs still need real behavior proof above when behavior changes.

</details>

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No

What is the highest-risk area?

- The Zalo target-id heuristic now treats any nonblank normalized Zalo target as a direct `chat_id`, so ordinary-looking strings can be sent directly instead of being rejected as unknown targets.

How is that risk mitigated?

- The behavior is scoped only to Zalo.
- Zalo documents `chat_id` as `String` and shows a dotted string example, so OpenClaw should not invent a narrower grammar.
- Blank and prefix-only inputs still fail normalization.
- Tests cover numeric, reported hex-like, documented dotted, prefixed, ordinary nonblank, and blank target shapes.

<details>
<summary>Risk guidance</summary>

Use this for author judgment that is not obvious from the diff. ClawSweeper can see touched files, but it cannot know which behavior you think is risky, why the risk is acceptable, or what mitigation reviewers should verify.

</details>

What is the next action?

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

- Waiting on GitHub CI and maintainer re-review. Live Zalo delivery proof would require valid Zalo Bot API credentials; the included dry-run proof covers OpenClaw target resolution without sending a live message.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

- Addressed Vincent Koc's review on #93689 by removing the undocumented hex-only grammar, treating normalized nonblank Zalo `chat_id` values as opaque strings, and adding `abc.xyz` plus prefixed variants to the resolver test.

target.title: feat(browser): My Browser node-anchored turn routing (stacks on #93411)
target.body:
> **Stacked on #93411 — that must merge first.** Builds on the run-scoped `gateway.tools.byNode` primitive from #93411; the diff currently overlaps #93411's commits and will be rebased to the extension-only delta once #93411 lands. Draft until then.

## What this is for

**The headline use case: fill the long, annoying forms & questionnaires for me.** You're logged into some portal — a multi-page application, an expense claim, a detailed survey — and you'd rather not hand-type 30 fields. My Browser keeps you in your *own* Chrome (your session, your cookies, your tabs) and lets you tell the side-panel agent, in plain English, what you want; it fills the form in your real browser, **self-checks its work**, and stops short of submitting so you review first. The same loop draws on natural language, the agent's OpenClaw **memory** (your saved details), and **web lookup** for fields it needs to recall or research.

*Proven end-to-end* — one instruction ("fill this pizza order: Cameron Beeley, +44 7700 900142, …, large, bacon + extra cheese, 19:00, comment 'ring the doorbell twice', don't submit") → the agent navigated, filled **every field type** (text, radio, checkboxes, time, textarea), **snapshotted to verify its own work** ("Let me take a screenshot to verify the text fields too"), and left it unsubmitted for review:

![Form-fill demo — from one natural-language instruction the agent fills a multi-field form (text, radio, checkboxes, time, textarea) in the user's real browser, self-verifies via snapshots, and leaves it unsubmitted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anagnorisis2peripeteia/openclaw/proof-93680-assets/93680/mybrowser-formfill.png)

Everything below is the plumbing + hardening that makes this safe to run in your real browser. See **User-story traceability** (after the findings) for how each fix protects this use case.

## Summary

Makes "My Browser" a usable side-panel copilot on top of node-anchored tool-scoping. Four blocks:

**1. Node-anchored turn routing (the original core).** Routes the side-panel turn **through the hosting node** as an authenticated node-originated `agent.request`, so the gateway confines that turn's tools via `gateway.tools.byNode` (#93411), and pins the browser proxy back to that same node. Falls back to a direct gateway turn when no node hosts the bridge.
- Node-host event emitter (`node-event-emitter.ts`, re-exported via `plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime`); extension bridge forwards the side-panel `agent.request` via an `onAgentRequest` callback threaded from `server-lifecycle`; browser tool pins to the turn's `hostingNodeId`.

**2. Browser-copilot persona as a system prompt.** `server-lifecycle` injects `BROWSER_COPILOT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` as `extraSystemPrompt` on every node-originated side-panel `agent.request` (server-side, not client-injectable). Without it the agent tends to refuse browser tasks / fetch over HTTP; with it, it acts through the browser tool, defers only CAPTCHA/2FA/payment, and won't reload a page it's already on.

**3. Side-panel UX (`sidepanel.js`/`background.js`).**
- **Per-tab agent sessions** — deterministic key per pinned tab (`…:thread:tab-<id>`), so each attached tab has its own resumable conversation; "+ New session" resets the thread.
- **Live tab-context injection** — each turn carries the pinned tab's current URL+title, so the agent knows where it is without a tool round-trip and won't re-navigate a page it's on.
- **Streaming render fixes** — render the gateway's authoritative full text (no duplicate/garbled deltas), render line breaks, and split inter-tool commentary into separate persisted bubbles with a `→ <tool>` step line per tool call (the panel opts into `tool-events`).

**4. Bridge reliability.**
- **Page-only target announce** — only real `page` targets are announced to Playwright; worker/`blob:`/service-worker/cross-origin-iframe child targets are dropped (they were announced as phantom pages, hanging the next snapshot ~47s on heavy pages like signup flows).
- **Per-turn CDP keepalive** — reuse the cached CDP connection within an idle TTL, force a fresh reconnect after a gap; skip the per-op throwaway health-probe when a live connection is cached.
- **Idempotent `attachTab` + `getTargetId`** — re-attaching an already-connected tab no longer crashes Playwright with a Duplicate-target error; the panel can resolve a tab's CDP targetId to pin turns to it.

Out of scope: the `gateway.tools.byNode` primitive itself (#93411). The node-bridge driver uses its own literal `extension-bridge`, distinct from the legacy `extension` → `existing-session` value (whose doctor migration is preserved), so there is no deprecation collision.

## Linked context

Depends on #93411 (gateway-core `byNode`). Related #93347 (closed — superseded by the authenticated-node approach).

## Review findings addressed (local ClawSweeper / Codex review, head 11b72146a8)

Local + public ClawSweeper / Codex review rounds flagged the items below; all are resolved or explained:

1. **[HIGH] Unauthenticated extension bridge** (`extension-bridge-server.ts`) — **fixed.** When `gateway.auth.token` is configured, the `/extension` relay handshake must present a matching HMAC on `?token=` (recomputed server-side via WebCrypto, mirroring the extension's `deriveRelayToken`) or the socket is rejected (close 1008); tokenless loopback stays trusted-local. Proven live on the deployed build — `no-token → 1008`, `wrong-token → 1008`, `correct-HMAC → accepted` — plus 4 unit tests (`extension-bridge-server.auth.test.ts`).
2. **[MED] Hard-coded `DEFAULT_TOKEN`** (`sidepanel.js`) — **fixed.** Removed `test-token-for-container`; tokenless loopback now omits auth instead of sending a placeholder credential.
3. **[high] node-event emission on the public SDK** (`plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime.ts`) — **fixed** (`04d6d08b3b`). `emitNodeGatewayEvent` (and the install primitives) are removed from the public plugin-SDK barrel and moved to a dedicated **private** entrypoint `node-gateway-events-internal` (mirroring `ssrf-runtime-internal`): built for the bundled first-party bridge but excluded from public package exports, so a third-party plugin cannot install an emitter or forge node-attributed events. The extension package-boundary checks (`no-plugin-sdk-internal`, `no-src-outside-plugin-sdk`, `subpaths-exported`) all pass. (The private-subpath form as first implemented broke **runtime** resolution — found via live deploy, fixed in `b3e840c785`; see #14.)
4. **[P1] macOS toggle writes invalid config** (`ConfigStore.swift`) — **fixed.** Added `browser.priorDefaultProfile` to the config schema so the My Browser toggle's state write validates against the strict `browser` object.
5. **[P1] `driver:"extension"` collided with the legacy migration** — **fixed** (`677c875a8e`). The branch had repurposed the legacy `driver:"extension"` literal (which the doctor migrates to `existing-session`, Chrome MCP attach) for the new node-bridge mode *and* deleted that migration, so the doctor would silently rewrite a new-mode profile and legacy upgrades broke. Fixed by giving the new mode its own literal **`extension-bridge`** (zod union + refine, public type, the input-side resolver, the macOS toggle) and **restoring** the deleted `extension → existing-session` profile migration. `doctor-legacy-config` migration test passes; build clean. (The rename initially left the relay gate on the dead `extension` literal — found via live deploy, fixed in `f4f56efa2e`; see #15.)
6. **[P1] Dependency-graph change** (`pnpm-lock.yaml`) — **stacked-base drift; rebase/approval-gated.** The bundled `chrome-extension/package.json` is `private` and adds **no runtime dependencies**; the only lockfile changes are upstream override bumps (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `hono`, `aws`, `acp`) carried by the #93411-stacked base, not this PR. They disappear on the rebase to the extension-only delta. Full resolution needs that rebase or maintainer dependency-guard approval — neither available pre-#93411.
7. **[P2] `config.example.json` relayPort** — **fixed** (`debaa45e3e`). Was `18790`; corrected to `18792` (`DEFAULT_EXTENSION_BRIDGE_PORT`) so the bundled example dials the right bridge port.
8. **[P2] relay URL throws under tokenless auth** (`background-utils.js`) — **fixed** (`e1d56a8aba`). `buildRelayWsUrl` threw on a blank gateway token, but `gateway.auth.mode:"none"` is valid; it now returns a tokenless `/extension` URL (the node bridge accepts it only when it also has no configured token, so a token-protected bridge still rejects it).
9. **[P1] Schema-invalid macOS profile** (`ConfigStore.swift:178`) — **fixed** (`1fe8fe6009`). The My Browser toggle wrote `{driver:"extension-bridge"}` but the zod profile schema requires `color`; the toggle now writes a `color` so the saved config validates. (Distinct from #4, which added `priorDefaultProfile`.)
10. **[P1] Copilot prompt dropped** (`server-node-events.ts`) — **fixed** (`1fe8fe6009`). `server-lifecycle` emits `extraSystemPrompt` on the node-originated `agent.request`, but the receiver's `AgentDeepLink` parser omitted the field, so the browser-copilot persona never reached the agent. Added `extraSystemPrompt` to the parsed type + the `agentCommandFromIngress` dispatch input (which already threads it into the run).
11. **[P1] Explicit relay host pointed at the gateway** (`background.js getRelayHost`) — **fixed** (`1fe8fe6009`). `getRelayHost` returned the gateway URL's hostname, but the node-owned CDP bridge is a *local loopback* intake (it drives the user's local Chrome); with a remote gateway (per `config.example`'s `wss://…ts.net`) the relay would dial the wrong host. It now defaults to `127.0.0.1`, with an explicit `relayHost` override for advanced setups.
12. **[high] Node-routing fail-open** (`sidepanel.js`) — **fixed** (`1fe8fe6009`). A failed node turn silently fell back to a direct (unconfined) `sessions.send`, dropping `gateway.tools.byNode` confinement. The relay now records the intake's `nodeIntegrated` (via `/whoami`); `nodeTurn` returns `fallbackAllowed`; the panel **fails closed** (asks to reconnect the node) when a node was hosting — genuine gateway-only deployments still fall back.
13. **[P2] Options page blocked tokenless loopback** (`options.js`) — **fixed** (`c99fd6ab78`). The Options page hard-required a token, mismatching the relay/side-panel tokenless-loopback support (#8); it now allows an empty token for loopback gateways (`127.0.0.1`/`localhost`/`::1`) while still requiring one for remote gateways.
14. **[P0] F3 seam broke runtime module resolution — found via live deploy** — **fixed** (`b3e840c785`). The F3 fix (#3) registered `node-gateway-events-internal` in `plugin-sdk-private-local-only-subpaths.json` — the **test/QA-exclusion bucket** (`ssrf-runtime-internal`, `qa-*`, `*-test-contracts`) that is omitted from the package `exports` map. In any **installed** package the bridge's runtime `import` threw `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`, so `ensureExtensionRelayForProfiles` never bound the relay (the error was swallowed by its own `try/catch`) and node-anchored My Browser silently failed. Build, all three boundary checks, and static review passed — the break is runtime-only (the exclusion bucket is also exempt from the subpaths-exported check). Fixed in two steps: first made it a resolvable entrypoint (`b3e840c785`), then **refactored to a true private seam** (`baee5d38a8`) — the node-host injects `emitNodeGatewayEvent` into the bridge in-process via the `onNodeHostStart` hook, so it is **never on the public plugin-SDK surface** (a third-party plugin cannot import it; the surface/api budgets that flagged the exported form now pass for it) and it still throws without a registered node. `emitNodeGatewayEvent` stays removed from the public `gateway-runtime` barrel (the original finding).
15. **[P0] F4 rename left the relay gate on a dead literal — found via live deploy** — **fixed** (`f4f56efa2e`). `ResolvedBrowserConfig.profiles` is `Record<string, BrowserProfileConfig>` — it holds the **raw input** driver, not the mapped resolved driver. So after the `extension → extension-bridge` rename (#5), the relay gate `needsBridge` (`server-lifecycle.ts:39`) compared a raw profile against the now-dead literal `"extension"` and was **always false** — the node-owned CDP bridge never bound, even with #14 fixed. Gate on the input `"extension-bridge"`. (`config.ts:552` and `profile-capabilities.ts:27` are correct — they operate on the mapped/resolved driver.) Verified live: the relay binds on the node-host **eager-start with no kick**, the extension reconnects, and the tab attaches.
16. **[high] Node-turn status failure could bypass confinement** (`sidepanel.js`) — **fixed** (`12b9e03fa1`). The `catch` around the `nodeTurn` message treated a *rejected* `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` (background worker/relay unreachable) the same as a gateway-only deployment and fell through to a direct, unconfined `sessions.send`. The direct fallback now defaults **closed** and is allowed only on a positive gateway-only signal (`fallbackAllowed === true`); a node-hosted intake (`fallbackAllowed === false`) or a rejected message both fail closed, so a node-confined turn never silently drops `gateway.tools.byNode`.
17. **[high] node identity not surfaced on the bridge `/whoami`** (`server-lifecycle.ts`) — **fixed** (`1ce3dccc87`). `ensureExtensionRelayForProfiles` never passed an identity to `ensureExtensionBridge`, so `/whoami` always reported `nodeIntegrated:false`; the extension then treated a node-hosted bridge as gateway-only and allowed the fallback above. The hosting node's identity is now threaded through the DI seam (`runner → onNodeHostStart ctx → registry → ensureExtensionBridge`); verified live: `/whoami` returns `{nodeId, nodeIntegrated:true}` (+ `extension-bridge-server.whoami.test.ts`).
18. **[P1] browser CLI status didn't surface the `extension-bridge` driver** — **fixed** (`c03c0c3585`, refined `fc4fac3a29`). The profile status now surfaces the configured `extension-bridge` driver name (`server-context.ts` reverse-maps the resolved `extension` 1:1; `ProfileStatus.driver` type updated). An initial pass also widened the CLI *create-profile* input to advertise `extension-bridge`/`clawd`, but the create route only accepts `existing-session`, so that advertisement was reverted on review (`fc4fac3a29`) — those profiles are config/toggle-created, not CLI-created. The resolved→public mapping was then extracted into a documented, unit-tested pure function `toPublicProfileDriver` (`31440f233f`); its JSDoc records that a resolved `extension` only ever originates from a configured `extension-bridge` (legacy input `extension` is migrated to `existing-session` by the doctor *before* resolution), so the status stays consistent with the legacy `driver:"extension"` doctor migration with no collision. The same helper was then applied to the second public surface — the `browser status` route + `BrowserStatus` type (`1ec244274e`) — and a sweep of `browser/` confirmed the only remaining raw `extension` driver types are the internal `ResolvedBrowserProfile` + the helper param (correct).
19. **[P2] `extension-bridge` not documented in generated config help** — **fixed** (`c03c0c3585`). The zod `driver` union had no `.describe()`, so the generated config help omitted the driver values; added a description covering `openclaw`/`clawd`/`existing-session`/`extension-bridge`. (Build + config-help-quality test + browser-tool tests green.)
20. **[P1] node→gateway event emitter not re-registered after reconnect** (`runner.ts`) — **fixed** (`fc4fac3a29`). `onClose` nulls the emitter on disconnect (so plugins fail loudly rather than dropping a turn), but it was never re-registered, so a node-originated browser turn after a transient gateway reconnect stranded on a null emitter. Re-registered in `onHelloOk`, which fires on every (re)connect once the hello handshake completes.
21. **[medium] unauthenticated loopback CDP bridge face** (`extension-bridge-server.ts`) — **hardened** (`b3533a10c5`). | User story | Protected by |
|---|---|
| Fill forms in **my own** Chrome session (cookies/logins/tabs) | node-anchored turn routing (Summary block 1); `driver:"extension-bridge"` drives the *attached* tab over the node-local CDP bridge |

target.title: fix(agents): treat codex exec_command as exec-like
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #93482.

Codex app-server exposes shell execution as `exec_command`, but OpenClaw's exec-like warning and mutation paths only treated `exec`/`bash` as shell execution tools. This meant a read-only Codex `exec_command` with a normal non-zero exit could fall through to the generic tool-error warning path instead of using the same compact behavior as native exec tools.

This PR adds a small shared exec-like tool-name helper and uses it in:

- tool-error warning policy and failure-signal classification
- tool lifecycle handling for command item/result paths
- mutation classification so Codex `cmd` input gets the same read-only shell detection as `exec`/`bash`

Mutating `exec_command` failures still surface a warning; only non-mutating exec-like failures keep the existing compact/suppressed behavior.

## Codex contract checked

I inspected sibling `../codex` source before changing this Codex-facing path:

- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/unified_exec/exec_command.rs` returns `ToolName::plain("exec_command")` from `ExecCommandHandler::tool_name()`.
- `codex-rs/code-mode-protocol/src/description.rs` documents nested shell calls as `await tools.exec_command(...)`.
- `codex-rs/core/tests/suite/request_permissions.rs` builds real model events with `ev_function_call(call_id, "exec_command", ...)` and `cmd` arguments.

## Verification

- `node node_modules/oxfmt/bin/oxfmt --write --threads=1 --config .oxfmtrc.jsonc src/agents/exec-tool-names.ts src/agents/tool-error-summary.ts src/agents/tool-mutation.ts src/agents/tool-mutation.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/payloads.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-mutation.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/payloads.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/failure-signal.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental false`
- `git diff --check`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Codex app-server `exec_command` is now classified as exec-like for the OpenClaw tool handler, mutation classifier, failure signal helper, and payload warning policy; a read-only `cmd` command that exits non-zero no longer gets a generic user-visible tool failed warning, while mutating `exec_command` failures still warn.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw worktree based on upstream `main` commit `4292f0fe7f`, with a sibling OpenAI Codex checkout inspected for the real `exec_command` tool contract. Dependencies were hydrated by the repo committer workflow and tests ran through OpenClaw's `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` and `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` wrappers.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-mutation.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/payloads.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/failure-signal.test.ts`; `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental false`; `git diff --check`.

Evidence after fix: Vitest passed 2 shards, covering 4 files and 178 tests. The added handler test feeds a production `tool_execution_start`/`tool_execution_end` pair with `toolName: "exec_command"` and `cmd: "rg ..."`, proving OpenClaw records `lastToolError.mutatingAction: false` for the Codex event shape. The added payload tests prove the non-mutating `exec_command` warning is suppressed and the mutating `exec_command` warning remains visible.

Observed result after fix: `exec_command` now follows the same exec-like policy as `exec`/`bash`; benign read-only non-zero exits are not surfaced as generic failed warnings, and side-effecting failures remain visible.

What was not tested: I did not run a full live Codex app-server model turn; this PR uses source-contract inspection from `../codex` plus OpenClaw production helper tests for the event-to-warning path.

target.title: fix(codex): project guardianWarning circuit-breaker notification
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the codex app-server event projector **silently dropped** the `guardianWarning` notification. Codex emits this notification when its guardian review hits its rejection circuit-breaker (3 consecutive or 10 total denials in a turn), right before ending the turn as `interrupted`. OpenClaw projected `item/autoApprovalReview/*` and `turn/completed` but had no case for `guardianWarning`, so the rejection-limit reason vanished and the turn degraded to a generic interruption with no indication of why.

Closes #101207

## Why This Change Was Made

- Added a `guardianWarning` case to the projector's notification switch and a `handleGuardianWarning` helper that emits an agent event on the `codex_app_server.guardian` stream with `phase: "warning"` and the warning `message`, alongside the existing `autoApprovalReview` handling.
- Because `guardianWarning` is **thread-scoped** — codex emits it with only `{ message, threadId }` and no `turnId` — it is correlated on the thread alone (mirroring how `hook/*` notifications bypass the turn-strict check). Without this routing, the turn-strict pre-switch filter would drop every `guardianWarning` before it ever reached the switch, making the handler dead code for real traffic.

A potential follow-up (not in this PR) is surfacing the warning in user-visible attempt metadata; that needs a UX-placement decision, so this PR ships the projection parity first.

## User Impact

Consumers observing codex turns (telemetry/audit/agent-event streams) now see the guardian circuit-breaker warning instead of a bare interruption, making it clear the turn was ended because guardian rejections hit the limit — not because of a tool failure or crash.

## Evidence

Regression test in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` sends a real `{ threadId, message }` `guardianWarning` payload (no synthetic `turnId`) and asserts the warning agent event is projected on the `codex_app_server.guardian` stream. Without the thread-scoped routing the notification is dropped and the test fails. Codex app-server shard is green (126 tests).

target.title: fix: gateway Crestodian chat on Codex-harness models reports its crestodian tool as missing
target.body:
Closes #101216

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users onboarding through the gateway Crestodian chat (macOS app, `crestodian.chat` RPC) with a Codex-harness default model (`openai/gpt-5.5`) would get replies like "I can't inspect your current OpenClaw status from here because the crestodian tool isn't exposed in this session" — the setup helper could not run status, doctor, config, or channel operations at all on that path.

The Codex app-server harness defers dynamic tools behind its tool-search namespace by default (`codexDynamicToolsLoading: "searchable"`), and `resolveCodexDynamicToolDirectNames` never registered `crestodian` directly. The system prompt requires the agent to act only through that tool, so the model correctly reported it as missing. The intended fallback-config override (`codexDynamicToolsLoading: "direct"`) was never applied on the configured-model path and, being a per-run config, never reaches the harness `pluginConfig` (resolved from the process-global config snapshot) anyway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ring-zero Crestodian runs carry exactly one OpenClaw tool, so hiding it behind tool-search is never correct. The fix registers `crestodian` as a direct tool spec whenever the run carries `crestodianTool`, using the existing per-run direct-names seam (same mechanism that keeps `agents_list`/`sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield` direct). This is config-independent and covers gateway + TUI, configured-model + configless-fallback paths uniformly. The now-redundant (and gateway-ineffective) `codexDynamicToolsLoading: "direct"` override in the Crestodian fallback backend config is removed so there is one canonical mechanism.

## User Impact

The Crestodian onboarding/setup chat can inspect and repair OpenClaw state again when the configured default model runs through the Codex agent harness (`openai`/`codex` providers). No config or behavior change for other runs; `message_tool_only` direct registration is preserved.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `registers the ring-zero crestodian tool directly in searchable loading` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts` proves a `crestodianTool`-carrying run emits a direct spec (no `namespace`/`deferLoading`) under default searchable loading; it fails without the fix.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts` — 118/118 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/crestodian` — 43 files, 287/287 passed.

target.title: feat(skills): background lifecycle curator for workshop-created skills
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop's capture ladder is complete (`/learn`, default-on suggestions, autonomous capture), but there is no maintenance half: agent-created skills accumulate forever with no usage tracking, staleness handling, or cleanup path. Issue #95516 describes the resulting skill bloat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a background lifecycle curator for **workshop-created skills only** (skills whose applied proposal has `createdBy: "skill-workshop"`; manually authored skills are never touched):

- **Usage tracking** — the existing `skill.used` trusted diagnostic event now persists aggregate per-skill usage (`skill_usage` table, shared state DB, Kysely). A trusted-listeners-only delivery path keeps accounting alive when optional diagnostics are disabled.
- **Lifecycle states** — `active → stale` (30 days unused) `→ archived` (90 days unused), fixed constants, zero new config keys. Archived skills are filtered out of skill snapshots via one query per snapshot build; **files are never moved, edited, or deleted**. Pinned skills bypass all transitions. Archived → active only via explicit restore. Lifecycle identity is the canonical skill file, so same-named skills across agent workspaces never collide.
- **Scheduling** — daily sweep owned by the gateway maintenance timers (same pattern as media cleanup: delayed initial run, in-flight guard, logged errors), with explicit persisted state in `skill_curator_state`. Disabled in manual-RPC gateway tests.
- **Overlap detection** — deterministic token-similarity report (workspace-scoped, no LLM, no config); suggestions only, merging stays with the operator through the normal proposal approval flow.
- **Surfaces** — `openclaw skills curator [status|pin|unpin|restore]` CLI with `--json` and gateway fallback; additive gateway methods `skills.curator.status` (operator.read) and `pin/unpin/restore` (operator.admin); warn-only doctor finding when the curator hasn't completed a sweep for 7 days.

Deliberately narrower than #95516's full proposal: no auto-optimization, no auto-delete, no config surface (fixed 30d/90d vs the issue's configurable 180d/365d).

## User Impact

Users with long-lived agents get automatic hygiene for accumulated agent-created skills: stale ones are flagged, long-unused ones drop out of context (recoverable at any time), and overlap candidates are surfaced. Manually authored skills, pinned skills, and all skill files on disk are untouched. No new configuration.

## Evidence

- All touched suites green on Blacksmith Testbox: [full run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28828318238) (curator lifecycle matrix — transitions, pinned bypass, archived-not-auto-reactivated, multi-workspace same-name skills, ghost-row pruning, workspace-scoped overlap; skills loading/snapshot filtering incl. state-DB-unavailable fail-open; gateway maintenance/close/runtime wiring; method scopes; doctor contribution; state-DB schema; CLI) and [privacy-fix rerun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28828913884) (diagnostic-events trusted-only delivery, tool-hook e2e path-free public payload assertions, curator).
- Structured review (Codex/gpt-5.5) ran to clean across three fix rounds; accepted findings fixed: multi-workspace skill-key collision wedging the sweep, mixed file/name usage scoping, absolute skill paths leaking to public diagnostic listeners, and skill loading hard-failing when the state DB is unavailable (caught on Testbox).
- tsgo core + core.test lanes clean; oxfmt clean; `pnpm docs:map:gen` regenerated.
- Docs: `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` "Lifecycle curation" section.

Scoped implementation of the retirement half of #95516 (commented there; issue asks for a broader system — see comment for what is intentionally out of scope).

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.36.2 to 4.36.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.36.3

No user facing changes.

Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.36.3 - 01 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.2 - 04 Jun 2026

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.19.3 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 9 April 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.15, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3837
  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.3. #3865

4.35.2 - 15 Apr 2026

  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable is deprecated and will be removed in May 2026. If you are affected by this, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #3795

... (truncated)

target.title: fix: pace delivery recovery after startup outages
target.body:
Closes #101058

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where startup delivery recovery could replay many already-eligible queued messages in a tight burst after an outage or restart. That burst can concentrate outbound sends against channel/provider rate limits even though each individual delivery is retried sequentially.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup recovery now applies a small shared pacing delay between actual replay attempts for outbound deliveries and session deliveries. Backoff skips, max-retry moves, reconnect drains, and first-entry recovery semantics stay unchanged. The pacing sleep is excluded from the active recovery budget, so a large already-eligible backlog is not deferred solely because recovery is sleeping between sends; genuinely exhausted recovery work still defers cleanly.

## User Impact

Queued messages recovered after a restart are replayed more gently instead of all eligible entries being sent back-to-back. This should reduce avoidable 429s and temporary outbound delivery failures after longer outages while preserving existing retry and reconnect behavior.

## Evidence

Before premise, source at base `60ce506712295e03d53cd4b91f4472f61d5971a6`: `recoverPendingDeliveries` sorted pending entries and immediately iterated them with `for (const entry of pending)` before calling `drainQueuedEntry`; `recoverPendingSessionDeliveries` had the same tight startup loop. There was no sleep, pacing helper, or jitter between eligible replays.

After behavior proof, real SQLite queue recovery via `node --import tsx --input-type=module` against this branch:

```json
{
  "spacingMs": 250,
  "summary": {
    "recovered": 2,
    "failed": 0,
    "skippedMaxRetries": 0,
    "deferredBackoff": 0
  },
  "deliveryTimes": [
    { "to": "target-a" },
    { "to": "target-b" }

}
```

target.title: fix(plugins): trust official npm-only ClawHub installs
target.body:
Closes #92452

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who install the official Microsoft Teams channel through ClawHub would have the channel crash-loop when it starts, because the official ClawHub install could not pass the 6.x keyed-store trusted-plugin gate.

The reported install path is:

```bash
openclaw plugins install clawhub:@openclaw/msteams
```

On current published OpenClaw, that install records official ClawHub provenance, but `msteams` remains an untrusted global plugin. When the channel opens keyed state during startup, the runtime rejects it with:

```text
[msteams] [default] channel exited: openKeyedStore is only available for trusted plugins in this release.
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The trust predicate now recognizes official ClawHub installs whose official external catalog entry is npmSpec-only, reusing the existing official install-record/catalog matching helper instead of adding a Teams-specific bypass.

The trusted path still requires the install record to match an official ClawHub source/channel/URL and the official catalog package identity for the plugin id. Community, private, custom-URL, mismatched-package, and unrecorded global installs remain untrusted.

This intentionally does not solve broader self-hosted or arbitrary local plugin trust. Those remain separate from this narrow official ClawHub provenance fix.

## User Impact

Users can install the official Microsoft Teams channel from ClawHub and have the channel start normally instead of crash-looping at the keyed-state gate.

Official npmSpec-only ClawHub channel installs, including the same catalog shape used by Discord, can now satisfy `trustedOfficialInstall` when their install record and catalog identity match. Untrusted install sources still cannot access trusted keyed-state APIs.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(signal): retry debounce flush on reply session initialization conflict
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the Signal channel, a DM sent shortly after a previous turn's reply completes hits `reply session initialization conflicted` and the debounce flush handler only logs the error and drops the message — with no retry and no user-visible feedback.

Slack received bounded retry-with-backoff for this exact error in #99647, and Telegram has equivalent handling (#96550). Signal's debounce handler (`extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts:653`) had not received the equivalent treatment — it only logged and dropped on this error.

Fixes #100944 (also related: #98234, #98416).

## Changes

### Production code — `extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts` (+35 lines)

| Change | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Import | `collectErrorGraphCandidates`, `formatErrorMessage` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/error-runtime` |
| Const | `SIGNAL_RETRY_FLUSH_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` |
| Const | `SIGNAL_RETRY_FLUSH_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 1_000` |
| Const | `REPLY_SESSION_INIT_CONFLICT_MESSAGE_RE` (regex matching the error message) |
| Function | `isRetryableSignalInboundError()` — walks `error.cause` chain, returns `true` when the conflict message is found anywhere in the graph |
| Function | `flushWithRetry()` — wraps `handleSignalInboundMessage`; on retryable error waits 1s and recurses (max 3 retries), otherwise throws immediately |
| Change | `onFlush` calls `flushWithRetry` instead of bare `handleSignalInboundMessage` |

### Tests — `event-handler.debounce-retry.test.ts` (3 tests, fake timers)

Unit tests that verify retry behavior deterministically with `vi.useFakeTimers()`:

1. **Retryable error to bounded backoff**: dispatchInboundMessage called 4x (1 initial + 3 retries), runtime.error logged after exhaustion
2. **Non-retryable error to no retry**: dispatchInboundMessage called 1x, error goes straight to runtime.error
3. **Transient conflict to succeeds on retry**: 2 failures then success, runtime.error NOT called

### Real-environment tests — `event-handler.debounce-retry.real.test.ts` (3 tests, real timers)

These tests run through the **FULL production pipeline** — the only mock is `dispatchInboundMessage` (necessary to inject the session conflict error, which is a timing race that cannot be triggered naturally in CI). Everything else is real:

- Real `createChannelInboundDebouncer` (not mocked)
- Real `onFlush` with real `flushWithRetry`
- Real `handleSignalInboundMessage` (context building, routing, reply pipeline)
- Real `delay(1000)` via wall-clock `setTimeout`

target.title: feat(context-engine): report compaction successors as typed session targets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Context engines that own compaction report their post-compaction successor session to the host through `CompactResult.result.sessionFile` — a raw file-path string. A bare path cannot say which agent/session it belongs to or what storage mode backs it, so every consumer re-infers identity from a path, and the contract cannot describe non-file-backed sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a typed successor contract: `CompactResult.result.sessionTarget` (`{ kind: "file", agentId?, sessionId, sessionKey?, sessionFile }`) makes storage mode explicit and carries precise identity. The delegate populates it; host consumers (`adoptCompactionTranscript`, `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook`, queued-compaction rotation detection) read target-first with the raw-field fallback centralized in one helper (`resolveCompactionSuccessorTranscript`). This matches the direction main already took for runtime params in `run-session-target.ts`.

`CompactResult` is a shipped plugin-SDK surface (exported via `plugin-sdk/index.ts`, present in release tag v2026.6.11, documented in `docs/concepts/context-engine.md` for third-party engine authors), so `sessionFile` stays populated and is marked `@deprecated` naming that shipped contract, with removal planned once typed targets are the only successor contract.

## User Impact

None for existing plugins — `sessionFile` keeps working unchanged. Engine authors get a typed, documented successor contract; docs updated accordingly.

## Evidence

- Consumer map verified: all in-scope `CompactResult.sessionFile` readers migrated (`run.ts` adoption paths, `compact.queued.ts` rotation detection, delegate producer); the four look-alike readers of the runtime `EmbeddedAgentCompactResult` type confirmed out of scope at each site.
- `context-engine.test.ts` updated bridge test + 2 new tests; 206/206 tests pass across the five suites exercising compaction adoption paths.
- Plugin SDK API baseline regenerated via the sanctioned `plugin-sdk:api:gen` for the intentional surface addition; `pnpm build` green (SDK export checks pass).
- oxfmt/oxlint clean; structured review (codex/gpt-5.5) clean, zero findings.

## Summary

- Add `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` to control which agents a specific agent may contact via session tools (`sessions_send`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `session_status`)
- When unset, the agent falls back to the global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` list; when set to explicit IDs, only those targets are reachable; `[]` isolates the agent from all cross-agent access
- The global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` continues to act as a participation gate (both requester and target must match it) before per-agent outbound rules are evaluated
- Outbound-only semantics: only the requester's override is checked, not the target's
- Replace `matchesAllow` with `matchesGlobalParticipation` and add `evaluateAccess()` returning a structured `AgentToAgentDenyReason` so all call sites produce context-aware error messages via `formatAgentToAgentAccessError()`
- Scrub deleted agent references from per-agent outbound allowlists in `pruneAgentConfig()`

### Example config (hub-spoke pattern)

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "agentToAgent": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["*"] }
  },
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "david",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["*"] } } },
      { "id": "spoke",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } },
```
